title.narrative: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation (Sector) Project

description.narrative: ADB has supported the government in improving water supply and sanitation services in 70 of the 176 small towns in Nepal through three small towns projects introducing continuous water supply, meeting national quality standards, and providing universal household connections with subsidized connections and affordable supply for poor and vulnerable households.

description.narrative: Inclusive and sustainable access to water supply and sanitation services in project municipalities achieved

320,000 people (including all poor and vulnerable)* in project municipalities have access to 24/7 piped water supply at 100 liters per capita per day, meeting the national drinking water quality standards (2018 baseline: 0) (*Vulnerable people are defined as those suffering the effects of marginalization within or outside their community because of their ethnicity, gender, caste, religion, disability, health, education, or socioeconomic status. For the project, this specifically includes Dalit, disabled, disaster-affected, marginalized, and endangered indigenous groups that are politically, socially, or economically excluded) Achievement: 397516 Progress/Status: At the project completion, project towns are supplying water (maximum 24/7, 100 lpcd) to 397,516 populations. This consists of the following: i. 329,999 from 20 new towns (with 164,391 women, 7,718 poor HHs, and 32,595 HHs of vulnerable group.
ii. 67,517 population from the functionality enhancement works in 29 towns (35,312 women population).
This will be assessed during the PCR mission. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Target value: 320,000

64,000 people (including all poor and vulnerable) in project municipalities have access to improved sanitation facilities (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 80778 Progress/Status: 80,778 people (including poor and vulnerable) in project municipalities have access to improved sanitation facilities through OBA toilets, Tikapur FSM & SWD, Charikot DEWATS, Bhojpur DEWATS projects and Katahariya SWD
This will be assessed during the PCR mission. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Target value: 64,000

Average time per day spent by women on water collection reduced to zero in project coverage areas (2018 baseline: to be established)** (**Expected to be determined by the end of the first year of project implementation.) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The average time per day spent by women on water collection was 79.07 minutes during baseline. Currently, all HHs have yard connection with zero time for collection of water in all projects area.
This will be assessed during the PCR Mission. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Baseline value: To be established

Water supply and sanitation facilities operate at full capacity and operation and maintenance costs recovery (2018 baseline: none exist) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: All WSS projects are built for a 20-year population design, but less than a quarter of that period has passed for most of the completed projects. Water demand is low to fully operate the facilities, so most projects are pumping intermittently to save cost.
For all projects, TDF has recommended the water tariff to recover the O & M cost and loan repayment. The WUSCs have fixed the water tariff, and loan repayment is being done.
This will be assessed during the PCR Mission. Data Source: National census; annual and quarterly progress reports by PMO and WUAs; periodic project surveys (including baseline and end-line surveys); and annual TDF report Baseline value: None existing
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: 20 WUSCs of registered WUAs formed with at least 33% women members and at least one woman in a key post (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 39.89 Progress/Status: 20 WUSCs of registered WUAs have been formed. The 20 WUSCs have a total 180 members with 70 women members (38.89%). In the WUSCs, the womens are in the following positions. • 2 womens in chairpersons • 8 womens in vice-chairperson • 4 womens in secretary • 7 womens in treasurer Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 20 climate-resilient subprojects that integrate GESI for future investments prepared (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 23 Progress/Status: 23 climate-resilient subprojects with GESI integration have been prepared for future investments. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: Business plans and tariff guidelines prepared for project WUAs and municipalities, assisted by the Institutional Support and Service Advisory Unit and TDF (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Business plans and tariff guidelines have been prepared for all WUAs/projects by TDF. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: GESI inclusive WASH plans, including priority investments for 20 project municipalities, prepared and approved by the respective municipality (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: 20 GESI inclusive WASH plans prepared as per NWASH guidelines for the service wards of the WSS projects in close coordination with municipalities. Other wards of the municipality are being done by municipality and planned by DWSSM. The prepared wash plans are under approval. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (ii) 16 sex segregated public toilets with adequate space for wash facilities and design friendly to differently abled people constructed, with septic tanks (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 18 Progress/Status: 18 sex-segregated public toilets were constructed, of which 17 designed with sufficient space for wash facilities and accessibility features to accommodate differently abled individuals. These toilets were equipped with septic tanks to ensure proper sanitation and waste management. Additionally, 1 mobile toilet was supplied to one project municipality, enhancing access to sanitation in areas where permanent facilities may not be readily available. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (ii) 20 water treatment plants, with an estimated capacity of at least 0.6 million liters per day each, constructed (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: All 20 water supply projects have successfully constructed a water treatment plant. Each plant has a capacity exceeding 0.6 million liters per day (MLD), ensuring sufficient treatment capability to meet the demands at the end of design period in the respective project service area. The cumulative capacity is 83.14 MLD. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iii) 60,000 connections for households to piped water supply, with subsidized connections for 6,000 poor and vulnerable households (including 100% poor households headed by women) (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 73724 Progress/Status: The project connected a total of 73,724 households to piped water supply. Of these, 59,771 were new connections and 13,953 were added through enhancements in various previously constructed town projects. Notably, the project prioritized support for poor and vulnerable populations by providing subsidized connections for 5,351 households identified as poor or vulnerable. This included poor households headed by women, ensuring equitable access to water supply services for those most in need. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iii) Two decentralized wastewater treatment plants constructed and operational (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Two decentralized wastewater treatment plants were constructed at Bhojpur and Charikot municipalities. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iv) 30 kilometers of stormwater drainage constructed (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 40.28 Progress/Status: 2 storm water drainage contracts in Katahariya and Tikapur subprojects. Both packages are completed with 40.28 km of storm water drainage constructed from 2 packages. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (iv) Climate and disaster risks*** factored in design of subprojects, as necessary (2018 baseline: not applicable (***Climate and disaster risks include seismic events.) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: The climate and disaster risks were considered while designing the subproject by: i. Seismic consideration, ii. Flood, drainage area and unstable grounds., iii. Crossings high above flood level, iv. Soil/Materials testing, v. Ground water/perennial water sources, vi. Extra boreholes, vii. High land location, viii Retaining/diverting walls, ix . Pipe protections, x. Recharge pits, and xi. Increased reservoir capacity xii Water treatment plants, Use of Smart technology for operation xiii Slope protection work xiv Fire hydrants Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: (v) Climate and disaster risks*** factored in design of subprojects, as necessary (2018 baseline: not applicable) (***Climate and disaster risks include seismic events.) Achievement: 24 Progress/Status: The climate and disaster risks were considered while designing the subproject by; i. Sewer pipes in stable ground ii.Away from Flood, drainage area and unstable grounds. iii.Materials testing iv.Ground water infiltration. v.Inspection hole cover vi.Sewer line protections vii.Sewer cleaning and Sludge pumping vehicles viii.Pavement improvements ix.Increased capacity x.Wastewater testing lab xi.Flow diverting chambers xii.Capacity development activities xiii Slope protection work Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: 1a. Water supply infrastructure established or rehabilitated in 20 subprojects in 19 municipalities: (i) 2,000 kilometers of water supply pipes installed or rehabilitated (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 2908 Progress/Status: A total of 2,908 (2,663+245) Km water supply pipes were installed or rehabilitated in 20 WSS and 29 enhanced water subprojects. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Water supply and sanitation infrastructure in project municipalities improved Indicator: 1b. Sanitation infrastructure improved in 21 project municipalities: (i) 2,500 toilets constructed through output-based aid for poor and vulnerable households (2018 baseline: 0) Achievement: 3210 Progress/Status: 3,210 toilets were constructed through output-based aid for poor and vulnerable households in 19 subprojects. Data Source: Annual and quarterly project progress reports by PMO and WUAs
Periodic reports by the Ministry of Water Supply

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 100 staff (33 of them women) of DWSSM, TDF, project WUSCs, and project municipalities reported stronger technical knowledge of smart utility and project management leadership (2018 baseline: to be established) Achievement: 109 Progress/Status: 109 staff from DWSSM, TDF, WUSC and municipalities participated and voiced stronger technical knowledge on smart utility management after the training. Of 109 participants, 41 (37.61%) were women. Similarly, 105 people of which 99 womens participated in the leadership training.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
Sample project surveys Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2026 Target value: 100 Actual value: 109

Output: Institutional and community capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 100,000 people (at least 50% women) covered by awareness campaign on water conservation practices and sustainable hygiene behavior, and 80% report greater awareness (2018 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: 226133 Progress/Status: Awareness campaign on water conservation practices and sustainable hygiene behavior participated by 226,133 participants of which 113,077 (50.00 %) are womens and 80% reported greater awareness. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports by PMO
Annual reports by TDF
